title: "Benchmark: supplementary checks"

<!--
Supplementary material for the Benchmarking section of the report
(vignettes/articles/report.qmd). Nothing here is a graded requirement: the
required comparisons (handout Table 4) are in the report. Like the report,
the agreement numbers are computed at render time from the installed
package, and the timings are read from the saved results of
inst/benchmark/benchmark.R.
-->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(nbzinbreg)
source(system.file("benchmark", "benchmark_functions.R", package = "nbzinbreg"))
specs <- bench_specs()
pairs <- list()
for (s in specs) {
  for (h in if (s$model == "NB") "analytic" else c("analytic", "numeric")) {
    pairs[[length(pairs) + 1L]] <- fit_pair(s, h)
  }
}
bench <- compare_pairs(pairs)
saved_file <- system.file("benchmark", "benchmark_results.rds",
                          package = "nbzinbreg")
saved <- if (nzchar(saved_file)) readRDS(saved_file)
prov_check <- if (!is.null(saved)) check_saved_provenance(saved$provenance)
fmt <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", formatC(x, digits = 2, format = "e"))
pair_label <- function(id) {
  id <- sub("_analytic_vs_numeric$", " (analytic against numeric Hessian)", id)
  id <- sub("_analytic$", " (analytic Hessian)", id)
  id <- sub("_numeric$", " (numeric Hessian)", id)
  gsub("_", " ", id)
}
```

The report's Benchmarking section compares the required quantities of the
project description: the coefficients, their standard errors, theta (NB) or
log(theta) (ZINB), and the log-likelihood, each with a pass/fail tolerance.
This article adds comparisons that are **not graded requirements**, so they
have no tolerances. They are shown with two measures of difference:

* the **absolute difference** |ours − reference|, the measure the
  requirements use;
* the **relative difference** |ours − reference| / |reference|, which
  puts quantities of different sizes on a common footing (a relative
  difference of 1e-5 means agreement to about five significant digits).

The data, formulas and settings are those of the report: our functions at
their default settings, `MASS::glm.nb()` and `pscl::zeroinfl()` with tight
tolerances.

## Standard errors of theta and log(theta)

`nbreg()` reports SE(theta) and `zinbreg()` reports SE(log theta), as the
references do. Their agreement with the references:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-se-theta
#| tbl-cap: "Standard error of theta (NB) and of log(theta) (ZINB, analytic Hessian), against the references."
#| echo: false
sup <- bench$supplementary
s1 <- sup[sup$quantity %in% c("SE(theta)", "SE(log theta)") &
            !grepl("_numeric$", sup$pair), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(Comparison = pair_label(s1$pair),
                        Quantity = s1$quantity,
                        `Abs. difference` = fmt(s1$max_abs_diff),
                        `Rel. difference` = fmt(s1$max_rel_diff),
                        check.names = FALSE), align = "llrr")
```

## ZINB with the numeric Hessian

`zinbreg()` computes standard errors from the analytic Hessian (matrix of
second derivatives) of the log-likelihood by default; with
`zinbreg_control(hessian = "numeric")` it differentiates the log-likelihood
numerically instead (`numDeriv::hessian()`). The option only changes how the
matrix used for the standard errors is computed: the EM iterations and the
gradient check that stops them are the same, so the estimates are identical
and this checks the standard errors by a second, independent route.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-numeric
#| tbl-cap: "ZINB fits with the numeric Hessian against zeroinfl(), and our analytic against our numeric standard errors."
#| echo: false
s2 <- sup[grepl("_numeric$|_analytic_vs_numeric$", sup$pair), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(Comparison = pair_label(s2$pair),
                        Quantity = s2$quantity,
                        `Max. abs. difference` = fmt(s2$max_abs_diff),
                        `Max. rel. difference` = fmt(s2$max_rel_diff),
                        check.names = FALSE), align = "llrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: avn
#| include: false
avn <- max(s2$max_abs_diff[grepl("_analytic_vs_numeric$", s2$pair)])
vs_ref <- min(s2$max_abs_diff[grepl("_numeric$", s2$pair) &
                                s2$quantity == "standard errors"])
```

`r if (avn < vs_ref / 10) sprintf("Our two Hessian methods give standard errors that agree with each other to %s, far more closely than either agrees with zeroinfl() (at least %s). The remaining differences from zeroinfl() therefore come from the small differences between the two packages' estimates, not from how the standard errors are computed.", fmt(avn), fmt(vs_ref)) else sprintf("Our two Hessian methods differ by up to %s in the standard errors, which is not much smaller than their differences from zeroinfl() (%s); this deserves a closer look.", fmt(avn), fmt(vs_ref))`

## Validity checks

Every comparison in the report and here is made only after these checks
pass for both fits of a pair. A failed check would be reported here with its
reason, and the comparison would be marked as not assessed.

```{r}
#| label: validity
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
for (id in names(bench$validity)) {
  cat("\n**", pair_label(id), "**\n\n", sep = "")
  v <- bench$validity[[id]]
  print(knitr::kable(data.frame(Check = v$check,
                                Passed = ifelse(v$passed, "yes", "NO"),
                                Detail = v$detail), align = "lcl"))
  cat("\n")
}
```

## Timing with the numeric Hessian

The numeric Hessian needs many more evaluations of the log-likelihood, so it
is slower. Timings are from the saved benchmark results (median of 10 runs,
with the range).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time-numeric
#| tbl-cap: "zinbreg() with the analytic and the numeric Hessian: computation time in seconds."
#| echo: false
if (is.null(saved)) {
  cat("The saved timings were not found in the installed package; run inst/benchmark/benchmark.R.")
} else {
  tm <- saved$timing[grepl("^zinbreg", saved$timing$fit), ]
  knitr::kable(data.frame(
    Data = tm$data_name, Fit = tm$fit,
    `Median (s)` = formatC(tm$median_s, digits = 3, format = "g"),
    `Range (s)` = sprintf("%s to %s", formatC(tm$min_s, digits = 3, format = "g"),
                          formatC(tm$max_s, digits = 3, format = "g")),
    check.names = FALSE), align = "llrr")
}
```

`r if (!is.null(prov_check)) (if (prov_check$status == "matches") prov_check$message else paste0("**", prov_check$message, "**")) else ""`
